response:
Diagnosis from generation 8: smoothing the distress leg was the right call — ShortfallVsChronicDebtCoverage is now the best all-round signal in the archive (FMB −4.44, alpha −4.5%, t = −4.42, Sharpe −0.51) *and* it improved coverage to 0.129, confirming that chronic rather than transitory inability to service debt is the operative constraint. Two other findings shape this final round: (i) the five-year downtrend in dp/at delivered the most reliable alpha t-stat of any single-channel signal (−4.55) though with a weaker slope and lower coverage, so level-deviation and trend are complementary statistics of the same policy drift; (ii) the sales deflator failed decisively (FMB −1.66), settling the deflator question in favor of assets, and stock-based distress blends keep buying alpha at the cost of the slope. With no generations remaining, this batch consolidates the two validated improvements (long-memory/trend accrual state × chronic coverage) and tests the last few aggregation choices that could plausibly lift both statistics together.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: LongNormShortfallVsChronicDebtCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 7)))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistent asset-life stretching measured against a seven-year norm, combined with several consecutive years of inadequate cash coverage of contractual debt, identifies firms whose reported profits depend on deferring a real expense they cannot afford to recognize.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The seven-year norm produced the archive's strongest slope among accrual constructions and chronic coverage produced the strongest overall result on the distress side, and the two changes act on different legs so they should compound rather than conflict. This is the most direct consolidation of the two best independently validated refinements.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: DepreciationDowntrendVsChronicDebtCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: A steadily declining depreciation rate is the signature of deliberate asset-life extension, and pairing that directional policy measure with chronically weak debt coverage should isolate the firms with both the motive and the demonstrated behaviour.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The trend construction generated the most statistically reliable FF5 alpha in the archive (t = −4.55) when paired with single-year coverage, so upgrading its distress leg to the chronic version that improved every other signal is the natural completion of that experiment. Its weaker slope was plausibly caused by noise in the annual coverage ratio rather than by the trend itself, which this specification directly tests.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: ShortfallVsFiveYearChronicCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: If chronic distress is what matters, extending the coverage-averaging window to five years should match the accrual leg's horizon exactly and capture entrenched rather than merely recent financial weakness.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Moving coverage from one year to a three-year average improved every statistic, so the persistence horizon of the distress leg is an open and unexhausted design parameter, exactly parallel to the norm-window question that produced the largest gains earlier. If five years overshoots, the deterioration will show that chronic distress becomes stale, which is itself the informative boundary of the mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: LevelAndTrendDepreciationEvidenceVsChronicCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), NEG(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that is both below its own depreciation norm and on a five-year downward path is far more likely to be genuinely stretching asset lives than one displaying only a level gap or only a drift, so combining the two statistics should reduce misclassification on the accrual dimension.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Level deviation carries the strongest slope while the trend carries the strongest alpha t-stat, which implies they contain partly distinct information about the same policy state rather than being redundant transformations. Earlier attempts to strengthen the accrual leg failed because they added an economically different channel (working capital, asset growth); this one stays inside the depreciation mechanism, which is why it has a better chance of helping.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: ShortfallVsChronicCoverageAndDebtLoad
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5)))), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 3)), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Chronic inability to service debt and a large contractual debt burden are complementary constraints, and once the flow component is smoothed the stock component should add tail information without the noise that previously destroyed the cross-sectional slope.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Stock-plus-flow blends have twice produced the archive's largest alphas (−5.3% and −4.4%) while halving the slope, and the most likely culprit is the noisy single-year flow measure being averaged with a persistent stock measure, creating an unstable composite ranking. Replacing the annual flow with the chronic three-year version aligns the persistence of the two components and is the last untested repair of a recurring failure mode.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: ProportionalShortfallVsChronicDebtCoverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5), RATIO(dp, at)), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 5))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ADD(ni, dp), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Expressing the shortfall as a fraction of the firm's own normal depreciation rate makes the accrual leg comparable across capital intensities, and combining that scale-free measure with chronic distress should give the cleanest specification of the mechanism.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The proportional shortfall matched the absolute version on alpha and Sharpe but was slightly weaker on the slope under single-year coverage; since the chronic coverage leg reduced noise in every specification it was applied to, this pairing determines whether the proportional scaling was genuinely inferior or merely obscured by a noisy conditioning variable. Together with Signal 1 it closes out the two remaining accrual-leg scaling questions in the final generation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
